summary: Three high-severity false statements: Corollary 6.8 omits the nonzero-lift condition for injectivity; Lemma 11.4 omits the character factor in root exchange; the review-added general Langlands classification mistakes P = G for temperedness even with nonunitary central twists. The first two are inherited from arXiv v1; the third belongs to the extraction. Existing recorded source gaps are not duplicated.

findings.claim: Corollary 6.8 is extracted as injectivity on all tempered nongeneric representations, including those with zero theta lift. The implication θ_J(π₁) ≅ θ_J(π₂) ⇒ π₁ ≅ π₂ is false without θ_J(π₁) ≠ 0. Neither its item nor E1–E52 supplies that hypothesis.
findings.evidence: Gan–Savin, arXiv:2102.00372v1, Corollary 6.8, p. 22 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00372v1#page=22; read 2026-10-01, page image checked), prints the unrestricted implication for representations that are “tempered and non-generic”. Its proof invokes Proposition 6.6, which requires a common irreducible quotient, hence a nonzero lift. Counterexample within the paper: take F = Q₅ and a cubic division algebra D/F. Choose a nontrivial unramified cubic character χ₀ of F× and put χ = χ₀ ∘ Nrd on PD×; it descends since Nrd(z) = z³ and is nontrivial. Proposition 7.1(i),(iii), p. 23, gives π₁ = Θ_D(1) = π_deg[1], a non-supercuspidal discrete series, and π₂ = Θ_D(χ), a nonzero nongeneric depth-zero supercuspidal. They are distinct, tempered and nongeneric (see also §3.1(iii) and §3.4(2)). Both have nonzero PD× lift. Theorem 6.1 therefore makes both big, hence small, PGSp₆ lifts zero. For J = H₃(M₂(F)), the extracted implication says π₁ ≅ π₂. The later Theorem 12.4(ii), p. 39, and Theorem 15.1(iii), p. 52, retain the nonzero condition; the sequel arXiv:2209.07346v2, Theorem 2.1(iii)(b), p. 8, restricts the injection to the nonvanishing locus. This is an error inherited from arXiv v1; whether the inaccessible published version repairs it was not established.
findings.fix: In cor-6-8 replace the last implication by 0 ≠ θ_J(π₁) ≅ θ_J(π₂) ⇒ π₁ ≅ π₂, with J fixed and both π_i tempered nongeneric. Equivalently restrict the map to representations with nonzero lift. Record the arXiv-v1 source issue with the counterexample and the version-access limitation; propagate the hypothesis to the human report and route 1’s design brief. The finite-length and conditional irreducibility clauses stay valid.

findings.claim: The extracted root-exchange map integrates ℓ(π(y)v) without multiplying by ψ_Y(y)⁻¹. For the stated arbitrary characters it is not a well-defined function on Y/(X ∩ Y), and even after choosing standard representatives it need not give a ψ_Y-equivariant functional.
findings.evidence: Gan–Savin, arXiv:2102.00372v1, Lemma 11.4 and its proof, p. 36 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00372v1#page=36; read 2026-10-01, both displays checked on the page image). The statement omits the character factor, but the proof’s intertwining operator includes ψ̄_Y(y). Direct counterexample: let H = F³ with (x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′) = (x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+xy′), and let π act on C_c^∞(F) by [π(x,y,z)f](t) = ψ(z+yt)f(t+x). Put X = {(0,y,z)}, Y = {(x,0,z)}, ℓ(f) = f(0), ψ_X(0,y,z) = ψ(z), and ψ_Y(x,0,z) = ψ(z+x). These are maximal abelian subgroups and their characters agree nontrivially on X ∩ Y = Z(H). With representatives (x,0,0), the extracted map is A(f) = ∫_F f(x) dx. It is translation invariant: A(π(x₀,0,0)f) = A(f), whereas membership in Hom_Y(π,ψ_Y) requires ψ(x₀)A(f). Choose ψ(x₀) ≠ 1 and f the indicator of a compact open set of positive measure. Furthermore changing a representative by z ∈ Z(H) multiplies the unweighted integrand by ψ(z), so it does not descend to the displayed quotient. Weighting by ψ_Y⁻¹ cancels this dependence and gives the desired character under translation. E1–E52 do not record this error.
findings.fix: State ℓ′(v) = ∫_{Y/(X ∩ Y)} ψ_Y(y)⁻¹ ℓ(π(y)v) dy, with compatible Haar measures; for unitary characters ψ_Y⁻¹ = ψ̄_Y. Explain descent using ψ_X|_{X∩Y} = ψ_Y|_{X∩Y}, and check ψ_Y-equivariance. Record a source issue for the discrepancy between the arXiv-v1 statement and proof and update the route/report. The special root-exchange application can use an unweighted integral only after specifying representatives on which ψ_Y is trivial; it does not justify the extracted general formula.

findings.claim: The review-added general Langlands classification says π is tempered if and only if P = G. Its hypotheses allow any connected reductive G and ν ∈ a_M*, so positive real unramified twists along the split centre remain possible when P = G. This falsely labels nonunitary central twists tempered.
findings.evidence: The item quantifies over connected reductive G and adds “π is tempered iff P = G”; Gan–Savin §3.4, p. 12, only discusses the centre-free group G₂. For the general classification see Silberger–Zink, arXiv:1407.6494v1, §§1.2–1.4, pp. 3–5 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.6494v1#page=4; read 2026-10-01): a_M* = R ⊗ X*(M), and regularity is “⟨ν, α⟩ > 0 ∀ α ∈ Δ(P)”. When G = GL₁ and P = G there are no roots, so this condition imposes no restriction on ν. Take σ = 1 and choose ν giving χ_ν = |·|_F. Then J(G,1,ν) = |·|_F is a smooth irreducible character of F× with P = G. It is not unitary, since its value at a uniformizer has absolute value q⁻¹ ≠ 1, and therefore is not tempered. Bernstein’s Representations of p-adic Groups (notes by K. Rumelhart), Chapter IV, §2.3, pp. 92–93 (https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~cass/research/pdf/bernstein.pdf#page=92), explicitly imposes compact centre before its temperedness/classification discussion; Proposition 43 just above separately requires unitary central character for the criterion modulo centre. The counterexample is an error in the extraction’s added generalization, not a newly identified claim of Gan–Savin.
findings.fix: Keep the general reductive-group classification, but replace the equivalence by: π is tempered exactly when P = G and ν = 0 (equivalently the positive real unramified twisting character is trivial). If the simpler P = G criterion is retained as a corollary, explicitly assume unitary central character or anisotropic centre. State how a_M* and its central summand are treated. Propagate this distinction to the source route for SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3 and to the report; do not attribute the extra general statement to Gan–Savin or put it in that paper’s errata.
